newsitem.title: USA: Rexene says problems not expected to last.
newsitem.headline: Rexene says problems not expected to last.

text.p: Rexene Corp chief executive officer Andrew Smith said several factors expected to hurt fourth quarter earnings are likely to ease by 1997.
"We're not forecasting these kinds of problems in 1997," he told Reuters after a speech to a Schroder Wertheim chemicals conference.
Rexene said earlier its fourth quarter earnings should remain at or near first and second quarter levels because of recent higher feedstock costs affecting the industry.
Earnings grew from $0.34 per share in the first quarter to $0.39 per share in the second quarter and $0.45 per share in the third quarter, but the growth is not expected for the fourth quarter.
Wall Street estimates for the fourth quarter were $0.45 per share.
"December will be a difficult month for our industry and for Rexene," Smith said.
However, he noted that prices for propane, a key raw material, have begun to ease from recent high levels.
Shares of Rexene were down 1/8 at 13-1/2.
